results.title: Coverage on an empty estate versus a principal who can see nothing
results.evidence: an estate with nothing filed and a reader who may see nothing both answer coverage 0.0 over 0 document(s) with the identical sentence: 'no document has been filed against any model you can see'. The first is a register with a gap and the second is a scope doing its job; a reader told the first when the truth is the second concludes the bank has filed nothing

results.title: Coverage against a `kind`- or `urn`-filtered search
results.evidence: a search narrowed to one model answers 0 match(es) over 0 document(s) searched and 1 unread, while `GET /api/v1/document-search/coverage` — the figure the search's own detail line tells a reader to check first — answers 0.5 over 4 document(s) across the whole estate. `coverage()` takes no `urn` and no `kind`, and the route passes neither, so the two numbers are about different corpora and nothing

results.title: Superseding every unread document with a text note
results.evidence: superseding an unread PDF with a 31-byte text note moved coverage from 0.4 to 0.6 (3 unread → 2) while the content it measured became unreachable: a term inside the superseded document now returns 0 result(s). The figure a reader is told to check before trusting an empty answer is improved by removing the documents it was counting

results.title: A quarantined or rejected attachment in the search results
results.evidence: a document the register rejected — state 'rejected', reviewed with 'wrong figure, do not use' — is returned by search with its text quoted back: 'the rejected figure is 99.9 percent'. `_candidates` yields every current attachment and filters only on `kind`, so none of the 4 states narrows the corpus. The hit carries `state`, which is honest and is not a filter: a reader searching for a figure find
